sections.title: Scope
sections.text: Covered US financial institutions must identify and verify the beneficial owners of legal-entity customers when a new account is opened. The duty applies to banks, broker-dealers, mutual funds and futures intermediaries. This digest is a paraphrase prepared for training and is not the legal text.

sections.title: Beneficial ownership prongs
sections.text: A beneficial owner is each individual who directly or indirectly owns 25 percent or more of the equity interests of the customer. Separately, one individual with significant responsibility to control or manage the entity, such as a chief executive or managing member, must be identified. Interests held through intermediate entities count towards the 25 percent threshold.

sections.title: Ongoing monitoring
sections.text: Institutions must keep customer information current on a risk basis and monitor accounts to identify and report suspicious activity. When monitoring reveals a change in ownership, the beneficial ownership record should be refreshed.

sections.title: Currency transaction reports
sections.text: Financial institutions must file a currency transaction report for cash deposits, withdrawals or exchanges of more than USD 10,000 in one business day. Several cash transactions by or for the same person are added together when the institution knows of them.

sections.title: Structuring
sections.text: Splitting cash into smaller amounts to stay under the reporting threshold is a federal offence even when the underlying money is lawful. Repeated deposits just below USD 10,000 are a classic indicator and should be considered for a suspicious activity report.

sections.title: Suspicious activity reports
sections.text: Banks must report transactions of USD 5,000 or more that they know or suspect involve illicit funds, are designed to evade reporting, or have no apparent lawful purpose. The report is generally due within 30 days of first detection.

sections.title: Beneficial ownership
sections.text: Member states require corporate entities to hold adequate, accurate and current information on their beneficial owners. A shareholding of more than 25 percent held by a natural person indicates ownership, and the information must be filed in a central register.

sections.title: Enhanced due diligence
sections.text: Obliged entities apply enhanced due diligence to relationships involving high-risk third countries and to complex or unusually large transactions with no apparent economic purpose. Measures include establishing the source of funds and obtaining senior management approval.

sections.title: Reporting to the FIU
sections.text: Obliged entities must promptly report suspicions to the national financial intelligence unit and hold a suspect transaction until they have done so. The customer must not be told that a report has been made.

sections.title: Customer due diligence
sections.text: Relevant persons must identify customers and verify their identity before establishing a business relationship. For a body corporate this includes identifying any individual who owns or controls more than 25 percent of the shares or voting rights.

sections.title: Enhanced due diligence
sections.text: Enhanced measures apply where the risk of money laundering is high, including relationships with persons established in high-risk third countries and transactions that are complex or unusually large. Firms must examine the background and purpose of such transactions and record their findings.

sections.title: Discrepancy reporting
sections.text: Where a firm finds a material difference between the ownership information it holds and the register of people with significant control, it must report the discrepancy to Companies House. The report should be made without delay once the difference is confirmed.

sections.title: Duty to report
sections.text: Staff in the regulated sector who know or suspect money laundering, or have reasonable grounds to do so, must tell their nominated officer. The nominated officer decides whether to submit a suspicious activity report to the National Crime Agency.

sections.title: Defence against money laundering
sections.text: A firm may ask for consent, known as a defence against money laundering, before carrying out a transaction it suspects involves criminal property. Telling the customer that a report has been made can amount to the offence of tipping off.

sections.title: Registered agents
sections.text: Registered agents in the territory must hold verified beneficial ownership information for every company they administer and produce it to the competent authority on request. A holding of 10 percent or more is treated as a beneficial interest for this purpose.

sections.title: Reliance on introducers
sections.text: Agents may rely on introducers for customer due diligence only where written terms guarantee that identification records will be supplied without delay. Responsibility for the adequacy of the due diligence stays with the agent.

sections.title: SARANOFF, Oleg Petrovich
sections.text: SARANOFF, Oleg Petrovich, also known as Oleg Saranov, born 2 November 1968, was designated on 11 April 2022 under the Eastern Trade Restrictions programme. He is described as a procurement agent for state-linked shipping interests. All assets of the designated person are frozen and no funds may be made available to him, directly or indirectly.

sections.title: TARVOS, Anatoly Sergeyevich
sections.text: TARVOS, Anatoly Sergeyevich, born 27 March 1961, was designated on 11 April 2022 as the controlling director of Volgamar Shipping. He is assessed to arrange vessel charters that circumvent trade restrictions. Listed persons are subject to an asset freeze and a travel ban.

sections.title: VOLGAMAR SHIPPING LTD
sections.text: VOLGAMAR SHIPPING LTD, a company registered in England and Wales, was designated on 11 April 2022. The entity is owned and controlled by TARVOS, Anatoly Sergeyevich and acts as a freight agent for restricted cargoes. Its stated address is Unit 4, 18 Harrow Wharf, London E14 9TQ.

sections.title: NORTHGATE PETROCHEM FZE
sections.text: NORTHGATE PETROCHEM FZE was designated on 19 July 2024 for brokering crude oil cargoes on behalf of restricted parties. A related company, Northgate Petrochem Ltd, is registered in the British Virgin Islands. Dealings with either company require a licence.

sections.title: Certificate of formation
sections.text: Meridian Trade LLC was formed in Delaware on 14 August 2019 under file number 6614093. Its registered office is 48 Harbor View Road, Suite 300, Wilmington, DE 19801. The company describes its business as wholesale import of industrial fasteners and marine fittings.

sections.title: Annual report: members and managers
sections.text: The 2025 annual report lists Thomas Reyburn as the sole manager of Meridian Trade LLC. The sole member is Halvorsen Holdings Ltd, a private company registered in England and Wales, holding a 100 percent membership interest.

sections.title: Incorporation and registered office
sections.text: Halvorsen Holdings Ltd was incorporated in England and Wales on 21 February 2019 with company number 11840265. Its registered office is 3rd Floor, 27 Cheapside Row, London EC2V 6AJ, an address used by a corporate services provider for several hundred companies.

sections.title: Officers and people with significant control
sections.text: Clara Penhallow is the sole director, appointed on incorporation. The register of people with significant control names Corvane Investments BV as a relevant legal entity holding 100 percent of the shares. No registrable individual is recorded.

sections.title: Registration
sections.text: Corvane Investments BV is entered in the Dutch trade register under number 72018833, with its seat in Amsterdam and its office at Herengracht 512-B, 1017 CB Amsterdam. Its stated activity is holding and financing of group companies.

sections.title: Shareholder and UBO register
sections.text: The sole shareholder of Corvane Investments BV is Blue Lantern Holdings Ltd of Road Town, Tortola. The UBO register entry, filed late in March 2025, names Viktor Halden as holding an indirect interest of more than 75 percent. Clara Penhallow is listed as managing director.

sections.title: Entity details
sections.text: Blue Lantern Holdings Ltd is a BVI business company, number 1987324, incorporated on 9 May 2018. Its registered agent office is Suite 7, Seabreeze Chambers, Road Town, Tortola VG1110.

sections.title: Beneficial ownership declaration
sections.text: The register of members shows Viktor Halden holding 75 of 100 issued shares and Ines Marlowe holding the remaining 25. Mr Halden is declared as the ultimate beneficial owner and sole director. Ms Marlowe is described as a passive investor resident at Flat 9, 12 Elgin Crescent, London.

sections.title: Certified identity documents
sections.text: A certified copy of Viktor Halden's Estonian identity card was supplied, giving a residential address of Narva maantee 88-14, 10127 Tallinn. The certification was made by a notary in Tallinn in October 2025.

sections.title: Customer due diligence
sections.text: Meridian Trade LLC opened a business checking account, number 4858372755, with Harbor Federal Bank on 3 September 2019. The beneficial ownership certificate named Thomas Reyburn as the controlling person and stated that no individual owns 25 percent or more. Expected activity is USD 150,000 to 250,000 a month from US distributors.

sections.title: Registered office and manager
sections.text: The file records the registered office at 48 Harbor View Road, Suite 300, Wilmington, and Thomas Reyburn's home address at 2214 Pelham Court, Newark, DE 19711. Mr Reyburn signed the account mandate as sole authorised signatory.

sections.title: Customer due diligence
sections.text: Halvorsen Holdings Ltd opened a business current account with Kingsmere Bank on 11 April 2019, signed by its director Clara Penhallow. The stated purpose is receipt of management fees from group companies. Ms Penhallow holds directorships in more than 40 unrelated companies.

sections.title: Customer due diligence
sections.text: Blue Lantern Holdings Ltd holds a US dollar corporate deposit account with Tortola Fiduciary Bank, opened on 20 June 2018 through its registered agent. Viktor Halden is the sole signatory. The declared source of funds is investment returns from European holdings.

sections.title: Summary
sections.text: Meridian Trade LLC was escalated after Harbor Federal Bank could not reconcile its beneficial ownership certificate with registry records. The ownership chain runs from Meridian through Halvorsen Holdings Ltd in the UK and Corvane Investments BV in the Netherlands to Blue Lantern Holdings Ltd in the British Virgin Islands. Each intermediate layer is wholly owned, so Viktor Halden's 75 percent stake in Blue Lantern gives him an indirect 75 percent of Meridian.

sections.title: Control assessment
sections.text: Although Thomas Reyburn is the named manager, correspondence shows that payment instructions above USD 100,000 were approved by Viktor Halden by email. The analyst assesses that Mr Halden controls Meridian Trade LLC in addition to owning it. Confidence in the control finding is moderate because the emails came from a third party.

sections.title: Funds flow
sections.text: Between January and June 2026 Meridian paid about USD 1.42 million to Halvorsen Holdings as monthly management fees. Halvorsen forwarded roughly 94 percent of each payment to Blue Lantern's account at Tortola Fiduciary Bank within three days. Alert ALT-2026-0311-01 fired on the March onward wire under the high-risk corridor rule.

sections.text: Kestrel Bay Trading Ltd was incorporated in England and Wales on 12 April 2021 with company number 13377210. The registered office is Unit 4, 18 Harrow Wharf, London E14 9TQ. Its nature of business is wholesale of fertilisers and non-ferrous metals.

Expected turnover was declared as GBP 60,000 a month from UK agricultural buyers. Director Oleg Saranov presented a British passport with date of birth 2 November 1968.
